effective.acceptance: The report's trace table has one row per requirement of the registrar sections of the LOGOS-SERVICE-DISCOVERY specification named in the context, in the document's order, each with a file:line in the unit or an explicit 'not in unit' / 'needs external evidence'. Every confirmed code finding has a new test in tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ that fails on the audited commit for the divergence it names. Prose-only findings are marked as such. The target implementation is unchanged.
effective.context:
Scope of this audit: the registrar role only. Trace the requirements of the spec's sections 'Registrar' (under Protocol Roles), 'Registrars' (Handling REGISTER requests, Handling GET_ADS requests), 'Waiting Time Calculation' (formula, scaling, occupancy score, service similarity, IP similarity score and its tree algorithms, safety parameter, lower bound enforcement), and the registrar-side rules of 'Message Validation' and 'Error Handling'. The rest of the spec is staged as reference for definitions and system parameters; do not trace it. Three sibling audits cover the advertiser, the discoverer, and the messages and signatures.

nim-libp2p is the Nim implementation of libp2p; the Logos service discovery protocol lives in libp2p/protocols/service_discovery.nim (entry module) and libp2p/protocols/service_discovery/. This unit is registrar.nim (REGISTER and GET_ADS handling, waiting time, the registrar table, the IP tree) and advertisement_cache.nim (the ad cache and its eviction). Other files of the protocol directory (types.nim, connection.nim, routing_table_manager.nim, the entry module's heartbeat) and the Kademlia routing table in libp2p/protocols/kademlia are outside the unit: read them where a requirement leads there, and mark behaviour that lives only there 'not in unit'. Record the resolved commit in the report.

The spec's 'Example ... algorithm' sections, the Appendix and the Implementation Notes are illustrative or recommended; a different algorithm that meets the normative MUST/SHOULD text is not by itself a divergence. Treat code comments that cite the spec as claims to check.

Running tests: tests are Nim unittest files named test_*.nim; tests/test_all.nim imports every test_*.nim under tests/ whose path contains the -d:path substring, so `make test service_discovery` compiles and runs everything under tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ (unit tests there, multi-node tests in component/, shared helpers in utils.nim). The gate puts nim 2.2.14 from /w/cache/nim-2.2.14/bin on PATH and runs `make test service_discovery`. Do not use nix: the flake's dev shell ships a nimble too old for the Makefile. New proof tests go in tests/libp2p/service_discovery/ as their own test_*.nim file named by finding id, are picked up with no other edit, and should copy the header and import style of an existing file there (SPDX header, `{.used.}`, the unittest wrapper from tests/tools/unittest). The build uses --styleCheck:error, so follow the existing naming. No external network is available to tests; a proof that needs a live remote peer is 'needs external evidence'.
